independence: Fresh isolated reader. I authored none of the frozen proposals. I read only the assigned brief, tasks_reader419.json, claims_reader419.json and the eight exact source_path files, plus tooling instructions; I did not read study cards, earlier reader outputs, authored calculations, plans, logs or project history. All numeric checks below were newly transcribed or recomputed from the supplied sources. No delegation and no claim/card edits.
source_access: All eight assigned source files were accessible: seven original PDFs and the saved primary Strommer article text. I made my own pdftotext extractions, rendered all 53 PDF pages at 150 dpi, and inspected relevant body pages and 13 numerical/table pages rendered at 300 dpi (including a Henry numerical-column crop). The saved Strommer text includes Methods, Results, Tables 1-4, Discussion, limitations and references but no figure images or individual-case dataset. Goncalves Dias supplementary flowchart/quality table and Borra supplementary material were not supplied. I did not browse or retrieve any other sources. Primary studies cited by the reviews, the Baldwin primary paper, later critiques/replies and clearer Henry originals were not independently read; their absence is an access limit, not a negative study finding.

results.note: Confirmed against printed pp.711-712 (PDF pages 2-3), including my 300 dpi Table 2 render. The category counts match; 62-8=54, 8/62=12.9032%, and 36/62=58.0645%. Table 2's post-mortem-negative hospitalized exception is real; the collective ante-mortem/post-mortem wording does not identify that person's earlier confirmation evidence. Results and Table 2 agree on antidepressants 8 and antipsychotics 5; the Discussion reverses those two counts, so the extraction appropriately follows the former. Recorded presence, being named in a cause, and being the only identified substance remain different measures. No individual causal adjudication protocol or sampling details are supplied.

Confirmed against printed pp.710-713 (PDF pages 1-4). I transcribed Figure 1's black-diamond confirmed-intake series at 300 dpi: July 2009 through March 2010 is 0,0,1,1,1,5,7,7,9, summing to 31. The controlled-drug criterion and spring-2010 classification sentence support the explicitly editorial reading; individual inclusion criteria are not given. The 95% is coroners' areas in England/Wales. Table 1's 18 self-inflicted deaths and the 11 suicide/8 open verdicts are separate un-cross-tabulated classifications. No rate or causal inference follows from these selected counts.

Confirmed at printed p.50 (PDF page 4) in my 150/300 dpi renders. The 46% is the review's second-hand CSF/blood detection comparison; no component case counts appear there. The collective reference range is 41-47; reference 41 on printed p.54 (PDF page 8) is Jenkins and Lavins on post-mortem CSF 6-acetylmorphine, a plausible lead rather than an explicit per-number citation. I did not open that primary paper and cannot validate its denominator, cases or analytical methods. This cannot be recast as 46% more deaths proved caused by heroin.

Correction refines 'three comparisons' to three cited publications without study-level comparison details, and carries a source-checked correction affecting the surrounding frozen claim: p.1768 says 12% were positive for diazepam, not 'diazepam-only' detection. The frozen statement/plain/magnitude should say diazepam-specific detection and should not imply sole detection or absence of other benzodiazepines. The original qualifications about timing, unmeasured tolerance, secondary reporting and absence of redistribution/site discussion are otherwise supported. I read none of the cited primary series.
results.corrected_extracted: The review lists time since last administration among determinants of blood morphine, reports deaths occurring hours after administration, and cites three publications in support of possible overlap with survivors without giving numerical survivor-comparison details. It argues that multiple-drug toxicity may better describe many deaths. Editors' appraisal: co-detection does not quantify causal contributions; timing and unmeasured tolerance limit concentration comparisons. The review does not discuss post-mortem redistribution or specimen-site explanations, so these must not be attributed to its authors. The Michigan comparison cites Monforte 1977; 1977 is the publication year, not a reported case-collection period. Separately, the polydrug section says 12% of fatalities in Monforte were positive for diazepam; this is diazepam-specific detection, not evidence that diazepam was the only substance or only benzodiazepine detected. Whole-group benzodiazepine detection is reported as 55%, 27% and 22% in three other cited sources. These are the review's secondary reports; the cited primary studies were not independently read.
results.corrected_locator: Pharmacology p.1766; Circumstances pp.1766-1767; True overdose p.1767; A new perspective: polydrug use theory pp.1768-1769 (diazepam sentence at bottom of p.1768); Research implications and Conclusions pp.1769-1770

results.note: The main sample, default rule and 802/235 split are confirmed. Correction adds a directly checked surrounding-claim error: Table 2 on p.71 prints methadone 107 in direct-overdose deaths (13%), not the frozen magnitude's 101/802. My arithmetic is 107/802=13.3416%. The 77.3%/22.7% figures are selected-record category shares; any ceiling/floor interpretation is a conditional editorial reading of the default rule, not a validated bound on true causes or an official-statistics error rate. Negative findings were not recorded and voluntary reporting supplies no completeness denominator.
results.corrected_extracted: The sample comprises 1,037 accidental drug-related deaths reported to NP-SAD in England and Wales for 2000. Cases with insufficient information or the specified intentional/no-verdict exclusions were removed. Two researchers independently identified/classified cases, with confirmation by an addiction specialist. Direct overdose was assigned where no evidence suggested another cause. Counts were 802 direct overdose and 235 in other categories: 74 acute physical events, 40 non-drug-related medical conditions plus 72 drug-related medical conditions (112 combined), 31 traumatic accidents and 18 acute infections. Editors' calculations: 802/1,037=77.3% and 235/1,037=22.7%. The default can place unrecognized alternatives in direct overdose; treating those shares as a ceiling/floor is conditional on the other category assignments being correct, not a validated bound on true causes, a misclassification estimate or a comparison with official statistics. Table 2 prints methadone implicated in 107/802 direct-overdose deaths (13% printed; editors' exact calculation 13.34%), not 101/802. The separate text's 4% sole implication does not establish sole detection. Reporting was voluntary, and negative toxicology findings were not recorded, leaving absence versus non-testing uncertain.
results.corrected_locator: Methods sections 2.1-2.3 pp.68-69; Results section 3.2 p.69 and Table 1 p.70; Table 2 methadone/direct-overdose cell and section 3.4 p.71; Discussion pp.72-73, including final paragraph

results.note: Confirmed against printed/PDF p.6, both 150 and 300 dpi. Section 5.1 says significant decreases in femoral 6-MAM across post-mortem time points, citing reference 16 without a size here. Section 5.2 separately relays variable post-mortem/ante-mortem opioid comparisons and significantly higher free morphine, with possible glucuronide hydrolysis. All listed timing, hospital-selection and matrix limits are present. These are a review's summaries; the cited studies were not independently read, and no correction factor or heroin-caused death count was established.

Confirmed at printed p.385 (PDF page 2), including my 150/300 dpi renders. The separate 7.72 mg/L plasma-MDMA case is a single short Results description with the stated symptoms. It does not give age, sex, sampling time or detailed follow-up; avoid upgrading it to a rigorously documented long-term survivor or tolerated range. I have not reproduced the reported ingestion amount.

Confirmed against printed/PDF p.6, both 150 and 300 dpi. Borra defines FB as femoral blood and reports higher MDMA/MDA FB concentrations compared with ante-mortem plasma/serum, without effect sizes in this passage. The proposed comparison limits track section 5.2 and correctly distinguish it from serial sampling solely after death. The underlying MDMA studies were not independently read.

Correction makes the decimal uncertainty operative and removes an unsupported blanket hospital-collection description. My own 300 dpi renders/crop show Table I case 5 as '0 11' with no visible decimal dot, and Table II cases 1-2 as '0 2'/'0 7' with missing/faint dots. The conventional readings in the proposal are plausible but cannot be repaired from an unprovided clearer source; the numerical ranges/comparison depend on them. The headers say mg/L plasma, but sampling times and collection circumstances are not specified for every measurement, and Results describes samples from road-accident scenes. Surrounding claim wording should preserve that uncertainty rather than state all values were hospital collections. Other clearly visible values and the one-below/one-within road-death comparison agree.
results.corrected_extracted: Tables I-III label analytical amounts as mg/L plasma. Table I's fatal MDMA entries are 0.36, detected, detected in blood/urine, 0.424, a scan entry appearing as '0 11', 1.16 and 1.26. The conventional reading of the unclear entry is 0.11, giving five numerical readings spanning 0.11-1.26, but its decimal dot is not visible in this supplied scan. Table II's five people who survived severe complications have readings conventionally transcribed as 0.2, 0.7, 0.97, 0.24 and 0.21; the first two appear as '0 2' and '0 7' with missing/faint decimal dots. One is a 1-year-old child's accidental exposure. Table III's three people who survived road accidents have MDMA 0.05, 0.34 and 0.15; the two people who died have 0.10 and 0.13. Conditional on those conventional decimal readings, the eight survivor values range 0.05-0.97, all five severe-case values lie within the five-value fatal range, and the road-death value 0.10 lies below 0.11 while 0.13 lies within. The decimal uncertainty remains unresolved by another source. These are selected clinical/accident cases; sampling times and collection circumstances for each measurement are not reported, and the Results describes samples from road-accident scenes. The plasma headers do not establish that every value was collected in hospital or from femoral autopsy blood. These comparisons do not supply a healthy ordinary-use baseline or a validated fatal cutoff.
results.corrected_locator: Methods and Results on p.385 (including road-accident-sample sentence); Tables I-III analytical-amounts, age and outcome columns and footnotes, pp.385-386; 300 dpi visual review of unclear decimal entries

Confirmed at printed/PDF p.2 in my 150 dpi render. The supplementary PRISMA flowchart and quality table were not supplied, so inclusion completeness and implementation of these methods remain unverified.

Confirmed from the saved primary article text's Methods and Introduction. Search date, English-language selection, exclusions, article-term coding, outcome and overlapping force/drug categories are all stated. The analysis is explicitly univariate. No standardized toxicology protocol or concentrations are presented for the pooled analysis, but that is not evidence that every source case lacked testing. Figure images are absent from the supplied text; this confirmation does not include their visual content or independently read underlying case reports.

Confirmed from saved Table 2, Methods and Discussion. Independent subtraction yields 94 deaths with some recorded force and 43 survivors, totaling 137, with 3 explicit no-force and 28 unknown-force cases. Exact percentages are 90.3846% and 67.1875%; Discussion's 67% agrees while Results' 68% differs. Initial Results also prints 138 force cases, inconsistent with the none/unknown totals; do not substitute that unreconciled numerator. Overlapping categories include sedation/TASER, and the authors explicitly cannot resolve the two deaths with no described restraint. No individual case data or Figure 2 image was available.

Confirmed from saved Methods, Analysis of outcome and Table 2. I transcribed cocaine 55/19, alcohol 16/6, marijuana 5/21, stimulants 28/24, and none noted 18/3, in 104 deaths/64 survivors. Cocaine OR=(55*45)/(49*19)=2.65843179, agreeing with printed 2.7. This is an unadjusted selected-case association, not a drug concentration comparison or causal drug-death count; 'none noted' is not a standardized negative test.

Confirmed as a description of the saved 2020 article's printed aggregates and internal mismatch.
